title: First bands: Golden Rule band, Young Tuxedo Band lineup
summary: He lists his first band's members and its change into the Young Tuxedo Band with its personnel.

bands.name: Golden Rule New Orleans Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You see the one that's still living?
Yes, the one's still living. And a fellow by the name of Bush Hall and Raymond Brown on trombone.
Well, I remember Lawrence used to talk about Bush Hall.
I mean any relation of the other halls like Edmund Hall and...

No, relations at all. Bush Hall. No, he had no relation at all. Let's see. We formed a...we first called the band the Golden Rule New Orleans Jazz Band, the Golden Rule Band. And we said we had Paul Bones, Eddie, Morrell, Lawrence Morrell, and we didn't have no piano during them days with the outfit. And later on, we formally made the band into the Young Tuxedo Band. Name it after Paul. That time it was called the Original Tuxedo Band with Bebe originally on trombone, which is the manager. And... Come right on through.
I'll leave this over there on tip on that. All right. That's all right. You can't hear it. You're talking about Bebe originally. Yeah, you know. And Papa Celestan.

Well, that time he used to...that we had the original Tuxedo Band. And then we used the title of the Young Tuxedo Band. Now that outfit consists of Dwight Newman on piano, and we had trained over to Paul Bent on trombone, Dennis Harris on saxophone and clarinet, Louis Contrell on saxophone and tenor sax and clarinet. And the regular rhythm section consists of White Newman piano, Lawrence Morale banjo, Eddie Morale bass, and myself drums. That was the regular rhythm. Eight pieces out.
